findings.title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user can be either an admin or the owner, not normally both as reported by these two helpers, so this expression is effectively always false and team admins/owners who are neither the booking organizer nor an attendee will always get a FORBIDDEN error. It should be `||`. (Also note `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` queries membership for team id 0 for personal bookings, which is a misleading fallback.)

findings.title: Guest list is not de-duplicated or case-normalized before insert
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters guests that exactly match an existing attendee email and non-lowercased blacklist entries; it does not de-duplicate the incoming array itself. The tRPC input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) also allows duplicates. A direct API call with `guests: ["a@a.com", "a@a.com"]` (or `A@a.com` for an existing attendee) will create duplicate attendee rows for the same booking, producing duplicate emails and corrupt attendee lists. Dedupe case-insensitively server-side and compare existing attendee emails case-insensitively.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against a lowercased list
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased when parsed from `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, but the incoming guest email is compared raw (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Any blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g. `Spam@example.com`) bypasses the blacklist and is added as an attendee, defeating the purpose of the environment variable. Lowercase the guest before comparison.

findings.title: Emails are keyed off the unfiltered input list, not the actually-added guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input array instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in this list decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` ("you were invited") or the "guests added" notification. If a submitted email was filtered out because it is already an attendee, that existing attendee incorrectly receives a brand-new booking confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable metadata
findings.body: Every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`) guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and accepts an `eventTypeMetadata` argument. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always sends to both host and attendees, so event types configured with `disableStandardEmails` will still send organizer and attendee emails, violating that setting.

findings.title: CalendarEvent is built without team info, so team hosts are never notified
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify co-hosts, but the `evt` constructed here never sets `team` (the booking query doesn't load the event type's hosts/users either). For team or round-robin bookings, no team member other than the booking owner receives the guests-added email, unlike the location-change flow which populates team members.

findings.title: ICS attachment lacks iCalUID/sequence, likely creating duplicate calendar entries
findings.body: The `evt` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` sets only `uid` and omits `iCalUID` / `iCalSequence` (both stored on the booking). The generated ICS is sent with `method: "REQUEST"`, so recipients' calendar clients will treat it as a new invite with a different UID rather than an update to the existing event, resulting in duplicate calendar entries for the attendees who already had the booking.

findings.title: findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0` throws an opaque 500 for bookings without a user
findings.body: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` will throw a Prisma `NotFoundError` (surfacing as an untranslated INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR to the client) for any booking whose `userId` is null, e.g. dynamic group bookings. Handle the null case explicitly with a proper TRPCError, or derive the organizer from the already-included `booking.user` relation.

findings.title: No guard against adding guests to seated, cancelled or past bookings
findings.body: The handler adds attendees to any booking regardless of `status` or `seatsPerTimeSlot`. For seated event types, remaining seats are derived from the attendee count and each real seat has a `BookingSeat` reference; inserting plain attendees here silently consumes seats without seat references, corrupting seat availability. For past or cancelled bookings (the "Edit" actions menu is also rendered for past confirmed bookings in BookingListItem), new guests receive a confirmation email and ICS for an event that already happened. Validate booking status and reject seated event types.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports its own package barrel, creating a circular dependency
findings.body: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports `MultiEmailLazy` -> `MultiEmail`. This import cycle can yield `undefined` components at runtime depending on module evaluation order, and it pulls the entire UI barrel into the dynamically imported chunk, defeating the purpose of the lazy wrapper. Import the components from their concrete module paths (e.g. `../components/button`, `../components/form`) as the other `form/*` components do.

findings.title: Error toast shows raw tRPC error code and the fallback message is dead code
findings.body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` is always a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` can never fall back to the friendly message. Users will see strings like `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission` (and `undefined: ...` when `err.data` is missing). Build the message from the translated key only, falling back to `unable_to_add_guests`.

findings.title: Invalid-email error never clears and empty list silently does nothing
findings.body: `handleAdd` sets `isInvalidEmail` to true on failure but never resets it to false on a subsequent successful validation or on dialog reopen, so the "Emails must be unique and valid" warning stays visible after the user fixes the input. Additionally, when the user removes all email rows (`multiEmailValue.length === 0`), clicking Add returns silently with no user feedback.

findings.title: Subject line dereferences attendees[0] without a guard
findings.body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw a TypeError if `attendees` is empty, and renders an empty name when the first attendee has no name (newly added guests are created with `name: ""`). Other organizer templates guard this (e.g. fall back to the organizer/team name). Since the email send is wrapped in a bare `catch` in the handler, such a failure would be silently swallowed and no organizer email sent.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely, so any failure to notify guests/organizers is undiagnosable in production. Use the project `logger` and include the error and bookingId.

findings.title: Copy-pasted comment claims a 40kb payload
findings.body: The comment "These are like 40kb that not every user needs" was copied from the PhoneInput/AddressInput lazy wrappers. `MultiEmail` is a small component with no heavy third-party dependency, so the comment misstates the reason for the dynamic import and will mislead future maintainers.

findings.title: New mutation has no tests
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` contains non-trivial authorization logic, guest filtering/blacklisting and email fan-out, but no unit or e2e test is added in this PR. At minimum the permission matrix (organizer / attendee / team admin / unrelated user) and the duplicate/blacklisted-guest filtering should be covered, since the authorization expression is currently inverted and would have been caught by a test.
